title: The Library of Alexandria: What We Actually Lost
description:
The greatest library of the ancient world did NOT burn down in one dramatic night of flames — it died slowly, quietly, while almost nobody noticed. Hundreds of thousands of scrolls, the collected knowledge of Greece, Egypt, and Babylon, gathered in one place for the first time in history. What we actually lost — and how we lost it — is a story nobody tells you right.

What fascinates me most is that the people of Alexandria were SO confident their knowledge was safe — and they were wrong. Knowledge is not automatically safe, not on papyrus, not on servers, not anywhere. If stories about the fragile, human side of history are your thing, subscribe to InkTime.

Watch next: our video "The Bronze Age Collapse: History's Greatest Mystery" — when the entire civilized world fell apart in fifty years, and nobody knows why. History rhymes.
